cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Acoustic – Relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

p.em: Example: We designed the new theater with excellent acoustic panels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tactile – Of or connected with the sense of touch.

p.em: Example: Her braille books offer a highly tactile reading experience.

cosy-blockquote.p: Navigate – Plan and direct the route or course of a path.

p.em: Example: It can be challenging to navigate a dark forest without a map.

cosy-blockquote.p: Orientation – The function of placing oneself in relation to one's surroundings.

p.em: Example: The tall lighthouse serves as a key orientation point for sailors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vulnerable ≠ Resilient – Susceptible to physical or emotional harm ≠ able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions.

p.em: Example: Sharing your secret thoughts makes you feel emotionally vulnerable, but showing courage helps you stay resilient.

cosy-blockquote.p: Symphony – An elaborate musical composition or a harmonious combination of sounds.

p.em: Example: The sounds of the forest at night became a chaotic symphony.

cosy-blockquote.p: Compassion – Sympathetic concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.

p.em: Example: She showed great compassion by helping the lost traveler find his way.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intimacy ≠ Estrangement – Close familiarity or friendship; closeness ≠ state of being alienated or separated in feeling or affection.

p.em: Example: Long conversations late at night build true emotional intimacy, while ignoring messages creates estrangement.

cosy-blockquote.p: Superficial ≠ Profound – Existing or occurring at or on the surface; shallow ≠ very great, intense, or displaying deep insight.

p.em: Example: He was only interested in superficial conversations about clothes, whereas she preferred profound discussions about philosophy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sensation – A physical feeling or perception resulting from contact with the body.

p.em: Example: The cold rain on my skin was a sharp and shocking sensation.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How would you navigate your city if you had to rely entirely on an acoustic map of echoes and footsteps?
★ What is the most welcoming sound you would listen for in your neighborhood?

If you couldn't see your partner or friends, how would you cultivate true emotional intimacy?
★ Does physical appearance actually get in the way of deep love?

How would you maintain your home's orientation and order if you couldn't visually inspect where items are placed?
★ What would be your biggest frustration if a visitor moved a single chair?

Would you feel more vulnerable in public spaces, or would your trust in human compassion increase?
★ Do you believe strangers are generally willing to guide someone in need?

How would you experience the sensation of a forest walk through your skin, nose, and ears rather than your eyes?
★ Is a scent sometimes more vivid and beautiful than a view?

How would your sense of fashion change if clothing choices were based on tactile pleasure instead of visual trends?
★ What texture makes you feel safest and most comfortable?

Do you think your judgment of people would become less superficial if you couldn't see their clothes, race, or age?
★ How much do visual biases corrupt our initial opinions of others?

How would you appreciate a crowded market if it sounded like a chaotic symphony of voices, steps, and clinking plates?
★ Does the eye simplify a room, while the ear makes it more complex?

How would you keep up with your hobbies and stay independent without a digital screen to look at?
★ What analog activity would you miss the most?

If you were suddenly given your sight back for just one hour, what is the single thing you would want to look at?
★ Would you look at a natural landscape or the face of a loved one?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Choose which perspective you would adapt to more easily: 🗺️ the echo maps Trusting spatial memory, acoustic patterns, fragrant indicators, and physical contact with cane and rails. 📱 the screen gaze Forcing your layout to be translated into active screen-readers, text-to-speech audio streams, and virtual braille pins.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In a blind-majority society, architecture would focus entirely on tactile walls, fragrant gardens, and specific acoustic chambers.
★ Why do modern designers only build for the eyes?

Our dependency on screens has made us emotionally superficial and unable to listen to each other.
★ Would removing visual distractions restore true human connection?

If you were blind, you would find it much easier to trust the compassion of humanity.
★ Does seeing the harshness of the world make us more cynical?

The future of technology lies in bone-conduction audio and sensory skin patches, rendering visual screens obsolete.
★ Are we moving toward an era of screenless digital interaction?

Blindness cultivates a much richer and more stable sense of self because it is immune to visual comparison.
★ Do mirrors do more damage to our self-esteem than they help?

If you had to navigate a crisis, a group of blind individuals would remain calmer than a group of sighted people.
★ Does visual panic spread faster than acoustic alarm?

The sensation of eating in total darkness makes the flavor of food infinitely more intense and memorable.
★ Why do we feel the need to look at our food before tasting it?

We would have much better social policies if politicians were forced to draft laws with their eyes closed.
★ Does visual evidence sometimes distract leaders from systemic truths?

A physical environment that is not accessible for non-visual orientation is a failed design, regardless of how beautiful it looks.
★ Should aesthetic appeal be secondary to functional accessibility?

If you were blind, your dreams would consist of rich, overlapping symphonies and textures that sight cannot comprehend.
★ Can the sleeping mind invent shapes it has never seen?

ul.li: Incorrect: A building would experience as a tactile map. → Correct: A building would be experienced as a tactile map. ((Grammar: Passive speculative voice required for passive subjects))
Incorrect: I had difficulty to orientation in the room. → Correct: I had difficulty orienting myself in the room. ((Lexicon: 'have difficulty doing something' requires a gerund))
Incorrect: The tactile maps are making by the architects. → Correct: The tactile maps are made by the architects. ((Grammar: Passive voice auxiliary takes a past participle form 'made'))
